# Mogharājamāṇavapucchā (Snp 5.16 (PTS Snp 216))

**ID:** Snp 5.16 (PTS Snp 216)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Mogharājamāṇavapucchā* ("The Questions of the Student Mogharāja", Snp 5.16, PTS Snp 216) is the sixteenth dialogue of the *Pārāyanavagga* in the *Suttanipāta* of the *Khuddaka Nikāya* [Hazra 1994]. In this discourse (commencing at verse 1116 in K. R. Norman's numbering), the student Mogharāja asks how one should view the world so as to escape the king of Death [Norman 1997]. The Buddha instructs Mogharāja to look upon the world as void (*suññato*), always remaining mindful, and to eradicate the self-view (*attānudiṭṭhim ūhacca*), by which means one transcends Death [Hazra 1994; Huynh Thi Ha Vy 2015].

 In canonical and post-canonical Pali literature, the text is expounded in the *Cūḷaniddesa* (*Mogharājamāṇavapucchāniddesa*, Cnd 19) and referenced in the *Peṭakopadesa* (Pe 2), *Nettippakaraṇa* (Ne 4), and *Kathāvatthu* (Kv 1.1). DharmaNexus records substantial Pali-internal text reuse with Cnd 19 (25 shared matches, particularly segment ranges §3.1–4.6), the *Mogharājattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 542, segments §2.1–4.6), Cnd 2 (*Pucchā*), the *Attadaṇḍasuttaniddesa* (Mnd 15), and the *Aṅguttaranikāye Ekakanipāta-ṭīkā* [DharmaNexus].
